concepts.source_guideline: Salvage Therapy for Prostate Cancer: AUA/ASTRO/SUO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Post-prostatectomy patient at high risk for recurrence but PSA is undetectable on standard assay
concepts.decision_point: Whether ultrasensitive PSA can be used for monitoring
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Use ultrasensitive PSA selectively when it will clarify high-risk recurrence monitoring
concepts.teaching_point: Post-prostatectomy surveillance can use ultrasensitive PSA selectively, but assay sensitivity should not create automatic treatment without clinical context.
concepts.source_section: post-prostatectomy PSA surveillance and biochemical recurrence monitoring

concepts.source_guideline: Clinically Localized Prostate Cancer: AUA/ASTRO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Localized prostate cancer patient undergoing prostatectomy wants preservation of erectile function
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Perform nerve-sparing when oncologically appropriate based on risk, tumor location, and function goals
concepts.teaching_point: Nerve-sparing is a risk-adapted surgical planning decision, not a universal step or a contraindication to cancer control.

concepts.source_guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/SUO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Initial TURBT intentionally leaves visible bladder tumor because complete resection was not technically achieved
concepts.decision_point: Next endoscopic management after incomplete initial resection
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Repeat transurethral resection or endoscopic treatment of remaining tumor if technically feasible
concepts.teaching_point: Incomplete TURBT is a staging and treatment-quality problem; visible residual tumor should be addressed rather than treated as routine surveillance.

concepts.source_guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/SUO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Low-risk NMIBC patient remains recurrence-free for five years of surveillance
concepts.decision_point: Whether surveillance must continue indefinitely on a fixed schedule
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Continue surveillance after five years only through shared decision-making
concepts.teaching_point: Low-risk NMIBC surveillance can be de-intensified after prolonged recurrence-free follow-up through shared decision-making.

concepts.source_guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones: AUA Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Recurrent calcium stone former has persistently high urinary calcium after diet counseling
concepts.decision_point: Medication choice for hypercalciuria-driven recurrent calcium stones
concepts.teaching_point: Medication prevention should match the persistent urine abnormality after diet measures; hypercalciuria points to thiazide therapy.
concepts.source_section: pharmacologic therapies for recurrent calcium stones

concepts.source_guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones: AUA Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Patient on stone-prevention therapy needs longitudinal surveillance for new stones or growth
concepts.decision_point: How to follow stone activity over time
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Use periodic imaging based on stone activity
concepts.teaching_point: Stone prevention follow-up includes imaging for stone activity, not only symptom checks or medication refills.

concepts.source_guideline: The AUA/SUFU Guideline on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Idiopathic Overactive Bladder
concepts.clinical_trigger: Patient starts an oral OAB medication and returns with uncertain benefit and dry mouth
concepts.decision_point: How to assess ongoing oral therapy
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Assess efficacy and side effects after starting pharmacotherapy and adjust treatment through shared decision-making
concepts.teaching_point: OAB medication follow-up should evaluate both symptom benefit and adverse effects rather than continuing ineffective therapy by default.

concepts.source_guideline: The AUA/SUFU Guideline on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Idiopathic Overactive Bladder
concepts.clinical_trigger: Patient has bothersome OAB symptoms and wants to compare antimuscarinic and beta-3 agonist treatment
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Offer antimuscarinic medications or beta-3 agonists after discussing side-effect profiles
concepts.teaching_point: Oral OAB therapy is preference- and risk-sensitive; class choice should account for adverse-effect profiles and patient priorities.

concepts.clinical_trigger: High-risk patient has persistent microhematuria and irritative voiding symptoms after a negative risk-based workup
concepts.decision_point: Whether urine cytology has a role after negative evaluation
concepts.correct_answer_concept: May obtain urine cytology when concern for carcinoma in situ remains
concepts.teaching_point: Urine cytology is not a routine replacement for cystoscopy, but persistent symptoms after negative workup can create a CIS-focused role.
concepts.source_section: urine cytology after negative microhematuria evaluation

concepts.clinical_trigger: Persistent microhematuria after prior evaluation that used renal ultrasound for upper tract imaging
concepts.decision_point: Whether additional upper tract imaging can be considered
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Consider additional imaging of the urinary tract when persistent or recurrent microhematuria follows ultrasound-based evaluation
concepts.teaching_point: Ultrasound-based hematuria evaluation may need escalation when microhematuria persists or recurs and clinical concern remains.

concepts.source_guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Male Chronic Pelvic Pain: AUA Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Male chronic pelvic pain patient has neuropathic burning pain without infection or obstructive voiding phenotype
concepts.decision_point: Medication class for neuropathic pain phenotype
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Consider neuropathic pain medications as part of multimodal management
concepts.teaching_point: CP/CPPS treatment should be phenotype-directed; neuropathic pain features point away from antibiotics and toward pain-modulating therapy.

concepts.source_guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Male Chronic Pelvic Pain: AUA Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Chronic scrotal content pain persists after conservative measures but pain is diffuse and not localized to epididymis or spermatic cord
concepts.decision_point: Whether to proceed directly to focal scrotal surgery
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Avoid focal surgery when pain localization does not support the target
concepts.teaching_point: Chronic scrotal content pain surgery depends on localization; diffuse pain should not be treated as a focal anatomic lesion.
concepts.source_section: chronic scrotal content pain surgical selection

concepts.source_guideline: Recurrent Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections in Women: AUA/CUA/SUFU Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Recurrent uncomplicated UTI patient asks about methenamine hippurate to reduce antibiotic exposure
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Methenamine hippurate may be offered as an antibiotic-sparing prophylaxis option
concepts.teaching_point: Recurrent UTI prevention can include selected antibiotic-sparing strategies when they match patient goals and evidence.

concepts.source_guideline: Recurrent Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections in Women: AUA/CUA/SUFU Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Woman with recurrent UTI has dysuria but culture is negative and symptoms do not respond to antibiotics
concepts.decision_point: How to manage possible alternative diagnosis
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Evaluate for alternative causes rather than escalating antibiotics
concepts.teaching_point: Recurrent UTI requires symptom-microbiology correlation; culture-negative nonresponse should trigger diagnostic reconsideration.

concepts.source_guideline: Early Detection of Prostate Cancer: AUA/SUO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Patient asks whether prostate cancer screening should continue at age 76 with excellent health and strong preference for screening
concepts.decision_point: Personalized screening beyond standard age ranges
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Individualize screening based on health, life expectancy, risk, and preference
concepts.teaching_point: Screening decisions in older patients should be individualized rather than using age alone as the only variable.

concepts.source_guideline: Clinically Localized Prostate Cancer: AUA/ASTRO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Localized prostate cancer patient asks whether urinary and sexual function should be documented before treatment choice
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Assess baseline urinary, sexual, and bowel function before treatment counseling
concepts.teaching_point: Baseline function changes how prostate cancer treatment harms are weighed and communicated.

concepts.source_guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/SUO Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: NMIBC patient has variant histology identified on TURBT
concepts.decision_point: How pathology features affect risk assessment and management discussion
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Recognize variant histology as a high-risk feature requiring expert pathology review and management escalation discussion
concepts.teaching_point: NMIBC risk is not stage alone; variant histology changes counseling and may justify early aggressive management discussion.

concepts.source_guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones: AUA Guideline
concepts.clinical_trigger: Recurrent calcium oxalate stone former has low urinary citrate but cannot tolerate potassium citrate tablets
concepts.decision_point: How to address persistent hypocitraturia when standard formulation is not tolerated
concepts.correct_answer_concept: Use citrate therapy or alternative alkali strategy tailored to tolerability
concepts.teaching_point: Hypocitraturia treatment is a urine-chemistry target, and formulation or alkali strategy may need adjustment for adherence.
